unmapped_findings: Hot forged specimen: the cast ingot was homogenized at 1100 °C for 2 hr and then hot forged to 50% thickness reduction in the temperature range 1050-800 °C, followed by air cooling to room temperature.

The hot forged specimen contains ~29 vol% austenite vs ~26 vol% in the cast specimen (Rietveld refinement of XRD) — a ~3% higher austenite fraction, attributed to some elemental partitioning during soaking at higher temperature that may increase the stability of the austenite phase.
A remnant dendritic structure is still visible in the hot forged specimen (blue arrow, Fig. 2e), possibly due to insufficient soaking and dissolution before hot forging.

Dilatometry performed on the hot-forged specimen (BAHR DIL 850; 4 mm dia × 10 mm cylinder; heating 10 °C/s; hold at 1000 °C for 5/15 min; cooling 1 °C/s) showed no significant deviation in the change in length apart from a slight deviation at ~600 °C; the two near-coincident traces were labelled '5 min holding time' and '15 min holding time'.

The δ-ferrite retained in the developed steel (including the hot forged state) is highly stable — its structure/morphology remains essentially unchanged after subsequent intercritical annealing; ~70 vol% δ-ferrite is present.
Nominal (designed) steel composition is Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C (wt.%); measured composition is Fe balance with Mn 7.79, Al 4.88, Si 0.84, C 0.2, P 0.03, S 0.03 wt.% (Table 1).
